key_insight: A neural operator framework can learn to solve free boundary problems with high accuracy and real-time speed, enabling rapid simulation of evolving interfaces such as tumour growth for clinical use.
problem_solved: Numerical solvers for free boundary problems are computationally intensive and slow for real-time or patient-specific applications; this work provides a fast, accurate surrogate that predicts both field solutions and moving boundaries.
method: Train a neural operator to learn the mapping from PDE inputs and initial/boundary conditions to solution fields and the evolving free boundary.
Couple field prediction with a boundary-evolution module for end-to-end learning of interface dynamics.
Validate and optimize the model for high precision and low-latency inference on tumour-growth simulation scenarios.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners with a physics-aware, high-speed surrogate for PDEs with moving interfaces, enabling real-time, personalized simulations and faster workflows for inverse problems and clinical decision support.
visual_elements: Schematic diagram: neural operator maps inputs (parameters, initial state) to solution field + evolving boundary
Benchmark chart: accuracy vs inference time comparing neural operator and traditional solvers
Time-series frames: predicted tumour boundary evolution side-by-side with ground truth
Icon cluster: speed (clock), accuracy (target), clinical application (stethoscope), PDE/physics (sigma or equation icon)
paper_title: Deep neural operator for free boundary problems
paper_authors: Zongjia Long, Qi Zhou, Aiqing Zhu, Dong Dai, Yiqun Liu
